title: Temporal-sample kernel annealing for transient clock headroom on mixed-MIG nodes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On mixed-sku fleets (H100/L40S/A10) with MIG partitions we observe transient thermal/clock headroom during short periods of low utilization (between bursts). Current kernel selection is static per-model/sequence-length and misses opportunities to use higher-throughput kernels for short decode windows, or conversely picks aggressive kernels that cause clock throttles and p99 latency spikes.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight 'temporal-sample kernel annealer' in the serving runtime that: 1) samples kernel candidates over short temporal windows (micro-batches / prefill->decode transitions), 2) tracks short-term headroom and anneals selection probability toward higher-throughput kernels when sustained headroom is observed, 3) preserves safety via hysteresis and rollback when clocks/thermal drop, and 4) is MIG-aware: respects slice capacity and avoids probing across MIG boundaries that increase contention.

Goals: Increase p50/p95 decode throughput during headroom windows without increasing p99 latency; avoid frequent kernel oscillation; keep probing overhead <2% CPU/GPU time per request on average.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Controlled experiments on H100, L40S, A10 show >=5% improvement in median decode token throughput for headroom windows (same prompt distribution) with <=3% regression in steady-state throughput.
2) P99 latency does not increase more than 2% vs baseline.
3) No new MIG cross-slice stalls observed in telemetry.
4) Canary rollout policy and automatic rollback on sustained error rate or SLO breaches implemented.
design_notes:
- Kernel candidate pool will be constrained to kernels validated for the model architecture + sequence-length buckets to avoid safety failures.
- Sampling window: 500ms by default, configurable per-pool.
- Annealing schedule: simple softmax over historical headroom score and kernel throughput estimate; decay factor to forget older samples.
- Hysteresis thresholds: require 3 consecutive positive headroom windows before switching to aggressive kernel; immediate rollback on thermal/clock drop beyond threshold.
- Probe budget: max 5% of requests may be used for exploratory kernel invocations; tracked per-GPU and per-MIG-slice.
- Fall-back rules: if kernel probe results in >5% token error (OOB/decoding failure), the candidate is blacklisted for 1 hour.
experiments:
- Bench 2025-02-18: microbench on isolated H100 80GB: 10k requests sampled; annealer reduced median decode time by 9% for sequences with decode length >128 tokens during headroom windows; p99 unchanged.
- Bench 2025-02-22: mixed MIG partition (2xL40S + 1xA10 in same rack, MIG slices active): observed 6% median improvement but occasional 1.5% throughput dip during aggressive probing; mitigated by reducing probe budget to 3%.
- Observed pathological case: bursty workload with inter-burst <200ms confuses annealer -> oscillation. Mitigation: increase minimum sampling window to 300ms and add oscillation dampening (exponential backoff).

blockers:
- Need updated GPU telemetry schema from infra (ENG-412987) to expose per-MIG clocks.
- Awaiting perf lab time on 2xL40S nodes week of 2025-02-24 (booking conflict).
decisions: Annealer implemented in serving runtime (not scheduler) to allow tight latency bounds
Probe budget capped to 5% then tuned to 3% after mixed-MIG tests
Use simple softmax annealer (no RL) to limit complexity and ensure predictable behavior
rollout_plan:
1) Lab validation on isolated nodes (H100/L40S/A10) -> merge to canary branch.
2) Canary: 5% traffic on non-critical customers for 48 hours; monitor p50/p95/p99 and error_rate.
3) Expand to 25% if metrics green for 24 hours.
4) Full fleet rollout with staggered region rollouts.
Rollback: automatic via runtime health check (SLO breach triggers revert flag).
notes:
Engineering trade-offs: simplicity vs optimality. We deliberately avoid per-request heavy optimization and focus on low-overhead probabilistic probing. This keeps code surface smaller and reduces risk on private deployments.
Implementation timeline: PoC -> 2 weeks; hardening + tests -> 1 week; canary -> 1 week.
